executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is dominated by two converging pressures: an active and escalating military confrontation with Iran, and a broad, sustained Russian information and cyber operations campaign. On the Iran front, the resumption of U.S. Central Command strikes against Iranian missile, drone, and radar infrastructure — conducted despite an active peace memorandum — signals a significant breakdown in diplomatic restraint, while Gulf States positioning themselves to lead diplomacy suggests Washington may be recalibrating its regional role even as kinetic operations intensify; the simultaneous erosion of Hezbollah's capacity as an Iranian proxy further compounds Tehran's strategic position. On the Russia front, the threads are tightly linked: Turla's deployment of new StockStay malware against Ukraine, the Russian fake tech-support credential harvesting scheme, and the FBI/CISA warning about targeting of commercial messaging platforms collectively reflect a coordinated, multi-vector Russian effort to sustain intelligence collection and information operations, with the Apple removal of VK apps adding a secondary front in the information space. The active exploitation of the PTC Windchill RCE flaw and FCC action on undersea cable infrastructure underscore that critical infrastructure remains under pressure from both criminal and state-affiliated actors, likely benefiting from geopolitical distraction. The overarching theme today is simultaneous crisis management across two major adversary tracks — Iran kinetically and Russia through hybrid means —

sections.title: Cyber
sections.intro: Russian cyber operations dominate today's threat landscape, spanning espionage malware, social engineering campaigns against messaging apps, and a diplomatic row over Apple's removal of Russian services.

items.headline: CISA and FBI warn of sustained Russian targeting of commercial messaging platforms
items.summary: An updated joint advisory from CISA and the FBI details ongoing Russian Intelligence Services phishing campaigns aimed at compromising accounts on commercial messaging apps. The update builds on a March 2026 warning, signaling the threat has not subsided and may be intensifying. Organizations relying on consumer-grade messaging tools for sensitive communications should treat this as an active, not theoretical, risk.

items.headline: Ukraine documents Russian fake tech-support scheme used to harvest messaging credentials
items.summary: Ukraine's SBU has detailed a sustained Russian operation in which actors posing as technical support staff socially engineered targets into surrendering credentials for their messaging accounts. The campaign complements the phishing tactics flagged in the CISA advisory, showing Russia is combining technical and human manipulation vectors. Ukrainian officials and partner governments are likely primary targets, making this a significant counterintelligence concern.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: Turla deploys new StockStay malware to deepen espionage operations against Ukraine
items.summary: Google threat intelligence researchers have identified StockStay, a new malware strain developed by Turla, one of Russia's most sophisticated state-linked cyber-espionage groups. The addition expands Turla's already extensive toolkit and indicates continued investment in persistent access operations targeting Ukrainian networks. Security teams should update detection rules and threat hunt for indicators of compromise associated with this group given the active conflict context.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: FCC moves to impose new licensing requirements on undersea cable infrastructure operators
items.summary: The FCC voted to strengthen regulations governing submarine cables, including an unprecedented proposal to require licensing for owners and operators of submarine line terminal equipment. Undersea cables carry the vast majority of global internet traffic, making them a high-value target for state actors seeking to surveil or disrupt communications. This regulatory push reflects growing concern about the physical security layer of critical internet infrastructure.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.intro: U.S. military action against Iran dominates today's geopolitical landscape, with cascading effects reshaping Middle East dynamics, proxy relationships, and regional power arrangements.

items.headline: U.S. Strikes Iranian Targets After Tehran Violates Hormuz Ceasefire
items.summary: Washington launched strikes against Iran following what it characterized as a ceasefire violation involving an attack on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The move marks a significant escalation and tests whether the existing diplomatic framework can survive direct military confrontation. Watch for Iranian retaliation options, potential Strait closure threats, and how Gulf states respond to renewed instability.

items.headline: Iran's War Costs Are Eroding Hezbollah's Value as a Strategic Asset
items.summary: The ongoing conflict has fundamentally altered Tehran's calculus on its proxy network, with Hezbollah shifting from a force-multiplier to a costly obligation the Iranian state struggles to sustain. This recalibration weakens a cornerstone of Iran's regional deterrence architecture built over four decades. The degree to which Tehran can reconstitute or redirect its proxy investments will define its post-war strategic posture.

items.headline: Gulf States Signal Readiness to Lead Iran Diplomacy as U.S. Steps Back from Primary Role
items.summary: Analysis indicates the UAE and Saudi Arabia have developed sufficient institutional capacity and strategic interest to manage Iran containment without relying on Washington as the primary broker, repositioning the U.S. as a guarantor of last resort rather than first responder. This reflects a broader restructuring of Middle East security architecture accelerated by the current conflict. The shift has significant implications for burden-sharing negotiations and U.S. force posture in the region.

items.headline: Colombia Elects Right-Wing President, Extending Latin America's Conservative Wave
items.summary: Colombia has voted in a Trump-aligned right-wing leader, continuing a regional trend that has seen multiple Latin American governments shift toward conservative, nationalist governance. The result represents a direct repudiation of outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro and his policies. Washington will likely leverage the election outcome to consolidate hemispheric alignment on trade, migration, and counter-narcotics priorities.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: U.S. forces resumed strikes on Iran while the Army accelerates drone integration and space organizational reforms signal broader modernization momentum.

items.headline: U.S. Central Command resumes strikes against Iranian missile, drone, and radar infrastructure
items.summary: CENTCOM struck multiple Iranian military sites on Friday, targeting missile systems, drone facilities, and radar installations. The resumption of strikes signals continued pressure on Iran's military capacity and raises questions about escalation dynamics and Iranian retaliation options. Watch for Iranian responses targeting regional U.S. assets or proxy activity across the Middle East.

items.headline: 101st Airborne soldiers employ drones for obstacle breaching, signaling a shift in infantry doctrine
items.summary: Soldiers from the 101st Airborne are using drones to drop grappling hooks and breach razor wire, with one officer arguing brigades will need 1,000–1,500 drones per week in sustained combat. The Infantry Squad Vehicle is also being explored as a mobile power source to keep drone systems operational in the field. This operational experimentation is pushing the Army toward treating drones as expendable consumables rather than managed equipment assets.

items.headline: Army establishes dedicated branch for space operations officers
items.summary: The U.S. Army has formally created a new branch to house its space operations officers, following the service's previously announced space vision strategy. The move institutionalizes space as a distinct warfighting function within Army force structure rather than a collateral specialty. This mirrors broader inter-service competition over space roles as the Space Force continues to define its own domain boundaries.

items.headline: Air Force seeks industry proposals for a long-range strike weapon exceeding 1,000 miles
items.summary: The Air Force held an Industry Day soliciting concepts for a next-generation weapon with both air-to-air and air-to-surface variants at ranges beyond 1,000 miles. The requirement reflects a strategic priority to hold targets at standoff distances that stress adversary air defenses, particularly relevant to a potential Taiwan contingency or high-end peer conflict. The dual-variant requirement is notable, suggesting the Air Force wants a single weapons family capable of prosecuting both aerial and ground threats at extreme range.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Today's intelligence picture is dominated by a rare direct U.S.-Iran kinetic exchange and a significant platform access dispute between Apple and Russia.

items.headline: U.S. Conducts Direct Strike on Iranian Forces Despite Active Peace Memorandum
items.summary: The U.S. military struck Iranian assets in response to an Iranian attack on a commercial vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first direct kinetic exchange since a peace memorandum was signed between the two countries. The strike signals that the memorandum has not deterred Iranian aggression against maritime traffic in one of the world's most strategically critical chokepoints. Analysts should monitor whether this triggers Iranian retaliation, shifts in Houthi or proxy activity, or formal diplomatic fallout from the memorandum parties.

items.headline: Apple Removes VK Ecosystem Apps from App Store, Russia Cries Political Censorship
items.summary: Apple pulled VKontakte, VK Music, VK Messenger, VK Video, Odnoklassniki, and Mail.ru from its App Store, effectively cutting off iOS users from Russia's dominant social and communication platforms. Moscow characterized the removals as politically motivated censorship, a framing that will likely fuel domestic narratives justifying further Russian internet sovereignty measures. This move has intelligence relevance as VK platforms have historically been monitored for open-source collection on Russian public sentiment and military-related discourse.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: The ICS/OT threat landscape today centers on active exploitation of industrial software, with CISA confirming the first known in-the-wild attacks against a widely used product lifecycle management platform.

items.headline: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of PTC Windchill Remote Code Execution Flaw
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-12569, a remote code execution vulnerability in PTC Windchill, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — marking the first confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of this flaw. Windchill is a widely deployed product lifecycle management (PLM) system used across manufacturing, defense, and critical infrastructure sectors, making a working RCE exploit particularly serious. Organizations running Windchill should treat patching as urgent and audit for signs of compromise, as PLM systems often hold sensitive engineering and design data.
